skill.name: env-config
skill.description: Guide Python projects through local environment configuration, validation, multi-environment setup, and password-based secrets encryption with UV.
skill.summary: Manage Python environment files and local secrets with documented workflows and a command-line helper.
skill.author: AutumnsGrove

security_audit.summary: Most static matches reflect the skill's legitimate purpose: local environment configuration, placeholder credentials, documentation, and test fixtures. Confirmed risks include remote scripts piped to shells, plaintext secret disclosure, unsafe permissions, and insecure secret output. No prompt injection or exfiltration intent was found, but 281 lower-priority analyzer matches remain outside this adjudication. Static review was capped at 400/681 representative findings; omitted static matches are unconfirmed, so automatic publishing stays disabled until manual review.

remediation.suggestion: Manually review the omitted 281 static analyzer matches or reduce bundled generated/vendor/reference content before enabling automatic publication.

remediation.issue: Installation examples pipe remote content directly into a shell.
remediation.suggestion: Download a pinned installer, verify its published checksum or signature, inspect it, and execute the verified local file.

remediation.issue: Several helper and troubleshooting paths print configuration or decrypted secret values.
remediation.suggestion: Print variable names and redacted fingerprints only, and require an explicit protected output file for decrypted data.

remediation.issue: The guide recommends mode 644 for .env files.
remediation.suggestion: Use mode 600 for secret files and verify owner-only access before reading or writing sensitive configuration.

remediation.issue: Passwords can be supplied through command-line arguments.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the password option and accept secrets through getpass, a protected file descriptor, or an approved secret manager.

remediation.issue: Examples create plaintext backups and can embed environment files in container layers.
remediation.suggestion: Avoid plaintext backups, inject secrets at runtime, and add all generated secret files to ignore and container-exclusion rules.

remediation.issue: Template masking relies on a narrow set of variable-name keywords.
remediation.suggestion: Default every value to an empty placeholder and allow only reviewed non-sensitive values to remain.

content.value_statement: Python teams can leak credentials or mix settings across environments. This skill provides local tools and guidance for structured configuration and secrets handling.
actual_capabilities: Explains UV project setup with python-dotenv, cryptography, Pydantic, and pytest dependencies.
Parses local environment files and validates required variable names.
Compares and merges environment files through a Python command-line helper.
Generates environment templates with configurable value masking.
Encrypts and decrypts user-selected secrets files with Fernet and password-derived keys.
Documents multi-environment, Docker, testing, and cloud secret-manager patterns.
limitations: The helper operates only on local files and does not provision cloud secret stores.
Output paths can overwrite files, and decrypted files do not receive enforced owner-only permissions.
Some diagnostics print sensitive values and require remediation before production use.
Template masking depends on variable names and may miss unconventional secret fields.

use_cases.title: Set Up a Python Project
use_cases.description: Create a consistent local configuration structure, dependency setup, template, and validation workflow.

use_cases.title: Separate Deployment Environments
use_cases.description: Plan distinct development, staging, and production settings with runtime injection for containers.

use_cases.title: Review Configuration Security
use_cases.description: Identify missing variables, placeholder secrets, unsafe storage, and configuration practices that need correction.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Set up environment configuration for my Python UV project. List required files, dependencies, variables, and validation steps.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner is starting a new Python application.

prompt_templates.title: Add Configuration Validation
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my required variable list and design startup validation for development and production. Do not print secret values.
prompt_templates.scenario: A developer needs predictable startup failures.

prompt_templates.title: Design Multiple Environments
prompt_templates.prompt: Design development, staging, and production configuration for this service. Explain precedence, container injection, testing, and secret isolation.
prompt_templates.scenario: A team is preparing several deployment environments.

prompt_templates.title: Audit and Migrate Configuration
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this configuration workflow for credential exposure, unsafe permissions, logging, backups, and rotation. Provide a prioritized migration plan.
prompt_templates.scenario: An experienced team is hardening an existing system.

output_examples.input: Plan environment configuration for a new Python API with a database and one external provider.
output: Create separate templates and local secret files.
Validate the database URL and provider key during startup.
Keep production values outside source control and inject them at runtime.

output_examples.input: Compare development and production configuration without revealing credentials.
output_examples.output: The comparison lists missing and changed variable names. Sensitive values are omitted, and permission issues are reported separately.

output_examples.input: Review a container deployment that uses an environment file.
output_examples.output: The review recommends runtime secret injection, excludes environment files from image layers, and verifies owner-only access on local secret files.

best_practices: Keep real secret files outside version control and container images.
Validate required names at startup without printing their values.
Use owner-only permissions and rotate credentials after suspected exposure.
anti_patterns: Do not pipe remote installers directly into a shell.
Do not print database URLs, API keys, or decrypted secret objects.
Do not copy environment files into images or broadly readable backups.

faq.question: Does this skill create environment files automatically?
faq.answer: It provides a helper for templates and merges. Review output paths and permissions before using generated files.

faq.question: Can it store secrets in AWS, Google Cloud, or Azure?
faq.answer: It documents integration patterns, but the helper does not provision or manage cloud secret stores.

faq.question: Does it support development, staging, and production?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance covers environment-specific files, precedence, testing, and runtime container injection.

faq.question: How are local secrets encrypted?
faq.answer: The helper uses Fernet with a key derived from a password through PBKDF2.

faq.question: Is the bundled helper safe for production without changes?
faq.answer: No. Remove sensitive output, enforce owner-only permissions, and address the audit remediation before production use.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The metadata declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
